answer: Concrete Sybil defense: each agent must lock a slashable stake tied to one provably unique identity. To field N clones an attacker posts N separate bonds, so cost scales linearly, and a single detected duplicate burns that clone's entire deposit. Imagine a juniper collateral note: one ember of fraud consumes it, and the harbor of rewards only admits stakes whose owners can be shown distinct, making mass identity fabrication prohibitively expensive.
